title: Twist: cluster selection, handedness, loops and skips

sections.title: Start with a longer model
sections.body: Use the Extrude workflow to make two separated 3-row × 6-column square-lattice clusters, each 256 bp long. All 3D images use Full representation. This lesson makes two successive 180° twists with opposite handedness, then generates and inspects loop/skip marks through NADOC’s own tools.

sections.title: Twist the first half
sections.body: Choose Tools → Twist, then click the original 18-helix cluster. Set Plane 1 to 0 bp and Plane 2 to 127 bp. Select Total twist, enter 180° and select Right-handed. The planes bound the twisted interval. After applying, reopen the saved part for a clean result view if the tool overlay remains dimmed (GUIDE-UX-008).

sections.title: Change handedness for the second half
sections.body: Choose Tools → Twist again and select the same cluster. Set planes 128–255 bp, Total twist 180° and Left-handed. These adjacent intervals demonstrate the two handedness controls along one bundle. Total twist specifies the rotation across the selected interval; Degrees/nm specifies rotation per unit length.

sections.title: Generate loops and skips
sections.body: Twist rotates the bundle cross-section along the selected interval. Add Loops/Skips creates the discrete insertion/deletion marks that accompany that design intent; use LOOP/SKIP to display the saved marks. The routing action requires crossovers, so first run Full Autostaple with Standard settings on this demonstration bundle.

sections.title: Inspect loops and skips in 3D
sections.body: Click LOOP/SKIP in the View toolbar (P). Orange loop markers indicate inserted bases and red × markers indicate deleted bases. The overlay follows the twisted geometry while Full remains selected.

sections.title: Inspect the same marks in the cadnano editor
sections.body: Open Origami Editor from the top bar. NADOC’s built-in cadnano-style path view shows the same document and loop/skip marks in a flat base-pair layout. Press F to fit, then zoom in to read individual symbols. The path view is a 2D topology view; the 3D window remains in Full representation.

steps.caption: Start with two 3×6 square-lattice clusters, each 256 bp long. Right-drag to view the clusters from the side, then press F to fit.
Choose Tools → Twist to open the tool and select a cluster.
Click the original 3×6 bundle to select its cluster. The second cluster provides a straight reference.
Set planes 0–127 bp, Total twist 180° and Right-handed. Inspect the preview, then click Apply.
The first half twists through 180° with Right-handed selected. Compare its rotating cross-section with the straight second cluster.
Set planes 128–255 bp, Total twist 180° and Left-handed. Inspect the preview, then click Apply.
steps.section: Change handedness for the second half

steps.caption: The second half twists through 180° with Left-handed selected. The two intervals show opposite twist directions within the selected cluster.
steps.section: Change handedness for the second half

steps.caption: Choose Tools → Routing → Full Autostaple to create the prerequisite staple routing and crossovers.
Keep Standard selected and click OK.
Choose Tools → Routing → Add Loops/Skips to generate marks for the square lattice and its twists.
Click LOOP/SKIP in the View toolbar to show the markers.
Full 3D view with loop and skip highlights on the twisted 3×6 bundle. Compare the marker distribution across the two twist intervals.
Click Origami Editor to open the same document in NADOC’s cadnano-style editor.
steps.section: Inspect the same marks in the cadnano editor

steps.caption: The cadnano-style editor shows the same routed bundle and saved loop/skip marks. Blue circles denote loops; red × symbols denote skips.
steps.section: Inspect the same marks in the cadnano editor

steps.caption: Scroll up over the path view to enlarge the symbols. Blue loop circles and red skip crosses appear directly on the routed strands; LOOP/SKIP remains enabled in the View toolbar.
